details.name: Generative AI for Software Engineering
details.exam_pattern: No local past papers are available. These questions follow the official learning outcomes; question wording, paper structure and marks are unknown.

families.title: Capabilities, limitations and failure modes
families.question: Official outcome: explain capabilities, limitations and failure modes of Generative AI across the software development lifecycle.
families.answer: Name the lifecycle task and the proposed AI contribution. Check its claims against requirements, code, tests and trusted sources; identify a failure mode and the accountable engineer.

families.title: GenAI across the software development lifecycle
families.question: Official outcome: apply tools effectively and critically to requirements, architecture and design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance.
families.answer: State the lifecycle stage, inputs and constraints. Use AI to draft options, then validate each artefact with stakeholders, tests, quality attributes and a named human decision.

families.title: Quality, readability, testability and maintainability
families.question: Official outcome: design, implement and evolve systems with GenAI-assisted workflows while maintaining software quality.
families.answer: Define observable behaviour and quality criteria. Review generated code for correctness, readability, coupling, errors and security; run focused tests including invalid and boundary cases.

families.title: Version control, experimentation and review
families.question: Official outcome: use version control and collaborative development practices appropriately, including safe experimentation, rollback and review.
families.answer: Keep experiments isolated and changes reviewable. Link the requirement, inspect the diff, test in a safe environment, document the decision and plan a complete rollback, including schema changes.

families.title: Evaluating AI-assisted workflows
families.question: Official outcome: evaluate workflows using suitable qualitative and quantitative criteria, while recognising uncertainty and bias.
families.answer: Define a fair comparison and a baseline. Measure task time, defects, review effort and maintainability as well as developer experience; explain bias, uncertainty and what the result cannot show.

families.title: Ethical, legal, security and professional risks
families.question: Official outcome: identify and manage risks arising from GenAI use in software engineering practice.
families.answer: Identify affected people and data, then the privacy, legal, security and professional risks. Specify permitted tools, minimised inputs, human review, audit evidence and residual risk.

families.title: Teamwork, communication and trade-offs
families.question: Official outcome: work effectively in teams and communicate GenAI decisions, trade-offs and risks clearly.
families.answer: Record context, alternatives, decision criteria, evidence, trade-offs and safeguards. Explain the decision to the team, assign accountability and set a review point.

cards.front: Why is fluent AI output not evidence of correctness?
cards.back: Fluency says nothing about fit to the actual system. Check claims against requirements, code, tests and trusted sources.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 1 and revision question bank

cards.front: How do hallucinated APIs differ from omitted edge cases?
cards.back: A hallucinated API invents a capability; an omitted edge case misses valid or failing behaviour. Verify the API in documentation and test boundaries.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 1 and revision question bank

cards.front: What should move an AI suggestion into an accepted engineering decision?
cards.back: Evidence from the real system, explicit criteria, tests and accountable human review.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 1 and revision question bank

cards.group: GenAI across the software development lifecycle
cards.front: What makes an AI drafted requirement testable?
cards.back: A clear stakeholder need, specific behaviour, constraints and an observable acceptance condition.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 2 and revision question bank

cards.group: GenAI across the software development lifecycle
cards.front: How should AI suggested architectures be compared?
cards.back: Compare against requirements, constraints and measurable quality attributes; verify claims and record trade-offs.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 2 and revision question bank

cards.group: GenAI across the software development lifecycle
cards.front: What must happen before an AI assisted change reaches deployment?
cards.back: Review the diff, verify requirements and tests, check security and compatibility, then use an accountable release gate.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 2 and revision question bank

cards.front: Why does high test coverage not prove generated code is correct?
cards.back: Coverage shows execution, not correct expected results or missing requirements. Check assertions, invalid inputs and boundary cases.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 3 and revision question bank

cards.front: What belongs in a quality gate for generated code?
cards.back: Focused unit and integration tests, static and security checks, readability review and a human explanation of the change.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 3 and revision question bank

cards.front: When should correct AI generated code still be rewritten?
cards.back: When its coupling, error handling or unfamiliar abstractions make it hard to maintain or inconsistent with the codebase.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 3 and revision question bank

cards.front: Why isolate AI generated implementation experiments?
cards.back: Isolation lets reviewers compare alternatives, reproduce results and discard a poor option without contaminating the main change.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 4 and revision question bank

cards.front: What does a complete rollback plan cover?
cards.back: Application version, database or data changes, configuration and verification that the previous behaviour is restored.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 4 and revision question bank

cards.front: What makes an AI assisted change reviewable?
cards.back: A bounded task, clear diff, linked requirement, evidence from tests and security checks, and a human rationale.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 4 and revision question bank

cards.front: Why is ticket speed alone a weak measure of AI assistance?
cards.back: It misses defects, review time, task difficulty and later maintenance cost.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 5 and revision question bank

cards.front: How can selection bias flatter an AI pilot?
cards.back: If easier tasks or more experienced developers enter the AI group, their better results may not be caused by the tool.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 5 and revision question bank

cards.front: Why is test compilation a weak test quality measure?
cards.back: Compiled tests may assert the wrong result or miss failures; inspect the oracle, coverage of decisions and fault detection.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 5 and revision question bank

cards.group: Ethical, legal, security and professional risks
cards.front: What is wrong with pasting a confidential log into a public AI prompt?
cards.back: It can expose customer data or secrets. Minimise and redact context and use an approved tool and access path.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 6 and revision question bank

cards.group: Ethical, legal, security and professional risks
cards.front: What must be checked before using an AI suggested package?
cards.back: Provenance, licence, approval, known vulnerabilities, maintenance and fit with the project.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 6 and revision question bank

cards.group: Ethical, legal, security and professional risks
cards.front: Who remains accountable for AI assisted engineering work?
cards.back: Named people who review, approve and can explain the decision, its evidence and its risks.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 6 and revision question bank

cards.front: What belongs in an architecture decision record?
cards.back: Context, alternatives, criteria, chosen option, evidence, trade-offs, consequences and review date.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 7 and revision question bank

cards.front: How should a team resolve conflicting AI suggestions?
cards.back: Compare both against requirements, architecture constraints and evidence, then record the human decision.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 7 and revision question bank

cards.front: What should a team agreement for GenAI cover?
cards.back: Permitted tools, data boundaries, review and testing expectations, documentation and escalation of uncertain output.
cards.evidence: Official outcome 7 and revision question bank

cards.group: GenAI across the software development lifecycle
cards.front: How should a team assess an AI-generated requirement from a prompt template?
cards.back: Check correctness against the real stakeholder need, completeness of constraints and acceptance conditions, and usefulness for planning. Record the prompt and output, then write an independent critique.

cards.front: What artefacts make an AI-assisted architecture choice reviewable?
cards.back: Show alternatives, a C4 container view for each, a score matrix against the stated quality criteria, an ADR for the choice, and your own critique of the decision.

cards.front: What evidence should accompany an agent-made one-fix pull request?
cards.back: Identify the changed file and PR, inspect the diff and tests, and retain the tool transcript so a reviewer can trace the proposed fix and the human decision.

cards.front: How do you improve AI-generated unit tests that merely compile?
cards.back: Review whether assertions check the right behaviour, find shallow tests and missing edge cases, then revise the prompt and rerun the tests. Judge test quality by fault detection, not generation volume.
